correctness_confidence.basis: All analytical claims in Theorems 2.2–2.6 and Proposition 2.7 check out mathematically, including the asymmetric RoM bound (8), Majorana-clique spectrum and purity 2^(1-n), W-state 2-marginal decomposition (13) and 3-Pauli bound 1+2/n, |CCZ> 4-clique value 2 vs 15/8 Pauli l1-norm, KCBS C5 top eigenvalue sqrt(5+2*sqrt(5)) and CG cut floor(5/2)=2, and the 4x4 Bell-basis eigenvalues 1+sqrt(5) of W_FT8 and 1+sqrt(3) of W_FT6. Numerical values in Table 2 and Figures 1–3 are mutually consistent.

novelty.basis: Synthesizes anticommuting Pauli cliques, Chvatal-Gomory integer-floor cuts, and signed frustrated commuting-triple atoms via F2-subgroup closure into a unified 3-tier dual framework for mixed-state Robustness of Magic. New specific contributions include the asymmetric shifted RoM formula (Theorem 2.2c), the 3-Pauli weight-<=2 n-qubit W-state marginal-magic certificate (Theorem 2.5), strict fixed-witness separation examples W_FT6/W_FT8 beating unsigned graph invariants (Theorem 2.6c), and the Subset-Dominance Dichotomy (Proposition 2.7).

reproducibility.basis: The manuscript specifies the exact witnesses, quantum states, rational bounds, certificate schema (SYMPLECTIC-MAGIC-CERT-1.0), and the full list of 16 Lean 4 theorem names and statements (Table 1). Deterministic runtimes, brute-force STAB_n check counts (6, 60, 1080), and exact numerical results across n=1..50 are reported clearly, though verification of the external GitHub Lean 4 and Python codebase lies outside this PDF-only assessment.

rigor.basis: Proofs of Theorems 2.2–2.6 and Proposition 2.7 are clear, self-contained, and rigorous, and Section 5 candidly delineates scope boundaries (external PSD realizability rho >= 0 and heuristic primal/dual search). Rigor is slightly tempered by minor notational abuses (beta_pm(W) depends on the decomposition, not solely W) and by the fact that the 16 Lean 4 theorems (Table 1) formalize the abstract combinatorial/arithmetic core rather than full complex Hilbert-space matrix mechanics.

significance.basis: Demonstrates a practical, zero-enumeration certification method for mixed-state Robustness of Magic and depolarizing noise tolerance up to n=32 qubits (bypassing |STAB_32| ~ 10^168.95) with exponentially fewer measurements than Pauli l1-norm on Majorana-clique states and O(1) weight-<=2 measurements on arbitrary-n W-states. Its impact is bounded mainly by the need for external heuristics to discover good atom decompositions on arbitrary unknown states and external certification of PSD realizability.

potential_errors: In Table 2 (jw_k65_n32) and Section 4.2, W_lb and R_cert are printed as 8.0622 whereas sqrt(65) = 8.0622577... rounds to 8.0623 at 4 decimal places; 8.0622 is a valid conservative rational lower-bound truncation (lo_p) from the radical-enclosure verifier, but differs by 1 ulp from standard rounding.

In Theorem 2.6(c), the parenthetical list of unsigned graph-theoretic stabilizer ceilings '(omega, chi_f_bar, vartheta, alpha_w)' on W_FT6 includes the clique number omega, which is not in general a stabilizer ceiling for weighted witnesses (unlike alpha_w <= vartheta <= chi_f_bar), even though omega = 3 happens to hold on W_FT6; the paper appropriately omits omega when discussing W_FT8.

In Section 2.1 and Definition 2.1, elements of F_2^{2n} and Hermitian Pauli operators in P_n are used interchangeably in notation (e.g., S_phi subset P_n alongside u in S_phi and u oplus v in S_phi, and omega(P,Q)=1).
strengths: Mathematically sound and cleanly proved two-atom conical duality and Chvatal-Gomory integer-floor framework (Theorem 2.2) yielding exact mixed-state Robustness of Magic and depolarizing-noise lower bounds without enumerating STAB_n.

Strong analytical exponential separation on mixed Majorana-clique states rho_{K_{2n+1}} (Theorem 2.4), certifying R >= sqrt(2n+1) and p_cert = 1 - 1/sqrt(2n+1) where the Pauli l1-norm is < 1 for all n >= 2.

Sharp resolution of the stabilizer-marginal problem for arbitrary n-qubit W-states using only three weight-<=2 Paulis {Z_0, X_0 X_1, Y_0 Y_2} (Theorem 2.5), while proving every 2-qubit marginal lies inside STAB_2.

Insightful strict 3-tier hierarchy (Theorem 2.6) and exact Subset-Dominance Dichotomy (Proposition 2.7) clarifying both why Tier 3 signed frustration beats all unsigned graph bounds on fixed witnesses (W_FT6, W_FT8) and why subset-selectable pure cliques dominate non-CG-rounded Tier 3 when individual Pauli expectations are accessible.
Transparent presentation of the zero-dependency Lean 4 theorem list (Table 1), exact-Q certificate verification pipeline, and clear Scope/Limitations (Section 5).
strong_novelty_candidates: Symplectic Atom-Cover and Chvatal-Gomory Rounding Theorem with asymmetric shifted Robustness of Magic lower bound (Theorem 2.2).
Three-Pauli weight-<=2 stabilizer-marginal magic certificate R(|W_n>) >= 1 + 2/n for all n >= 3 despite rho^(2)_{W_n} in STAB_2 (Theorem 2.5).

Signed frustrated commuting-triple atoms beating all unsigned anticommutation-graph invariants on fixed witnesses W_FT6 and W_FT8 paired with the Subset-Dominance Dichotomy (Theorem 2.6c and Proposition 2.7).
summary: The manuscript presents a zero-enumeration, exact-rational dual framework for certifying mixed-state non-stabilizerness and lower-bounding the Robustness of Magic (RoM) and depolarizing noise tolerance via two symplectic dual atoms over F_2^{2n}: anticommuting Pauli cliques and signed frustrated commuting triples, sharpened by Chvatal-Gomory integer-floor rounding (Theorem 2.2). It establishes worst-case RAC ceilings (Theorem 2.3), an exponential separation over the Pauli l1-norm on rank-2^{n-1} mixed Majorana-clique states up to n=32 qubits (Theorem 2.4), a three-Pauli weight-<=2 RoM certificate for arbitrary-n W-states whose 2-qubit marginals lie inside STAB_2 (Theorem 2.5), and a strict three-tier hierarchy with an exact Subset-Dominance Dichotomy explaining when signed frustration atoms outperform unsigned graph bounds versus when subset-selectable cliques dominate (Theorem 2.6, Proposition 2.7). All mathematical derivations and numerical benchmarks visible in the PDF are consistent and sound, supported by a transparently scoped 16-theorem Lean 4 abstract core and an exact-Q verifier design.
weaknesses: Table 1 reveals that the 16 Lean 4 theorems formalize the abstract symplectic/combinatorial/arithmetic core (for instance, theorem 15 is (n-2)+2+2 = n+2 > n and theorem 16 is floor(5/2)=2 and 2/5 < 1/2) rather than full 2^n x 2^n complex Hilbert-space matrix mechanics (such as stabilizer-state subgroup closure from density matrices, rho_{K_{2n+1}} >= 0, rho^(2)_{W_n} in STAB_2, spectral bounds of W_{C_5} and W_FT8, or spec(F_l) subset {-3,+1} for arbitrary quantum states rho >= 0).

The notation beta_pm(W) and hat_beta_pm(W) in Theorem 2.2 treats the stabilizer bounds as functions of W alone, whereas they depend on the chosen conical atom decomposition (y_j, C_j, z_l, F_l) in Eq. (5).

As noted in Section 5, discovering near-optimal atom decompositions for arbitrary unknown multi-qubit states still relies on external heuristic primal/dual search, and physical PSD realizability (rho >= 0) of state_expectations is an external assumption not checked by the certificate verifier.
Proposition 2.7 implicitly assumes W certifies magic (Tr(W rho) > beta_+(W), which also forces W_C != 0) when stating that dropping W_F strictly tightens the Robustness lower bound.
